summary: A short BBN note correcting and supplementing RFC 442 on IMP flow control. It points to two formal BBN publications as better sources and warns that the host-to-IMP interface had recently changed in ways that matter to people writing network control programs. It updates RFC 442.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC comments on RFC 442's description of IMPSYS flow control. It points readers, especially NCP programmers, to two formal BBN publications for further details.

questions: what sources did rfc 449 recommend for imp flow control
why was bbn report 1822 important to ncp programmers
which hosts needed to understand inter-imp acknowledgements
subtitle: A note directing readers to formal sources on IMPSYS flow control.

tldr.problem: The author says RFC 442's IMPSYS flow-control notes were reasonably accurate but could have cited BBN's formal publications.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 449 identifies two relevant publications and points out that the inter-IMP acknowledgement mechanism is described there as well.
tldr.outcome: The note says the acknowledgment is transparent to most Hosts but especially relevant to Very Distant Hosts. The unit metadata says it updates RFC 442.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 449 as Unknown and says it updates RFC 442. It is a pointer to additional flow-control documentation, not a new protocol specification.

sections.title: Comment on RFC 442
sections.content:
Dave Walden says the notes on IMPSYS flow control in RFC 442 seem reasonably accurate and cite a BBN quarterly technical report. He says BBN's two formal publications would have been better references.

The unit metadata says RFC 449 updates RFC 442.
sections.plainLanguage: The author considers the earlier notes reasonably accurate. He adds two formal sources that readers should consult.

sections.title: Recommended Publications
sections.content:
The first cited source is a paper by McQuillan and others, “Improvements in the Design and Performance of the ARPA Network,” in the Proceedings of AFIPS 1972 FJCC. The second is the December 1972 revision of BBN Report 1822, section 3, pages 17 through 35.

The note says BBN Report 1822 is particularly important reading for NCP programmers because things had changed somewhat.
sections.plainLanguage: The note names a conference paper and a revision of BBN Report 1822. It especially recommends Report 1822 to NCP programmers.

sections.title: Inter-IMP Acknowledgements
sections.content:
The inter-IMP acknowledgement mechanism discussed in the last section of RFC 442 is also described in the first publication. An almost identical mechanism appears in Appendix F of BBN Report 1822.

Walden says most Hosts need only understand the mechanism intellectually because it is transparent to network users, while the Report 1822 description is important to Very Distant Hosts.
sections.plainLanguage: Most Hosts do not expose the acknowledgement mechanism to users. The RFC says the details matter to Very Distant Hosts.

references.text: RFC 442, notes on IMPSYS flow control discussed by RFC 449.
